items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice as in the maximal-abelian-cover convention. Let $L=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_r\subset S^3$ be a nonempty oriented smooth link, with $r\ge1$, compact exterior $E_L$ formed by deleting the interiors of pairwise-disjoint chosen closed normal-disk tubes, and basepoint $b\in E_L$. For a knot, $r=1$ and $E_L=E_K$. The full meridian abelianization group is $H_L=H_1(E_L;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^r$, with the positive normal-disk meridians as its ordered basis. Choose a finite-rank free abelian group $H$ of positive rank and an epimorphism $\chi:H_L\to H$; write $\psi=\chi\circ\mathrm{ab}:G\to H$ for the induced map from $G=\pi_1(E_L,b)$. The identity choice $H=H_L$ is the full multivariable deck map; a coloring may identify its variables only through the explicitly stated map $\chi$. Let $\mathbb F$ be a field, let $d\ge1$, and let $\rho:G\to\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb F)$ be a representation. Put $\Lambda=\mathbb F[H]$, the commutative Laurent-polynomial ring with monomial basis $H$, and $Q=\operatorname{Frac}(\Lambda)$. On row vectors define the right $\mathbb F[G]$ action by $v\cdot g=v\rho(g)\psi(g)$, where $\psi(g)$ is central multiplication by its monomial in $\Lambda$. For a chosen finite based CW structure $X$ on $E_L$, orient and order its cells and choose one lift of each cell to the universal cover $\widetilde X$. The twisted cellular complex is

$$C_*^{\rho,\psi}(X;\Lambda^d)=\Lambda^d\otimes_{\mathbb F[G]}C_*(\widetilde X;\mathbb F),$$

and its fraction-field complex is $C_*^{\rho,\psi}(X;Q^d)=Q\otimes_{\Lambda}C_*^{\rho,\psi}(X;\Lambda^d)$. The lifted cell bases and the standard coordinate basis of $\mathbb F^d$ give the based $Q$-vector-space bases. If this fraction-field complex is not acyclic, define its twisted torsion to be $0$. If it is acyclic, choose in each degree a basis $\mathbf b_i$ of $B_i=\operatorname{im}\partial_{i+1}$ and lifts $\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{i-1}$ of $\mathbf b_{i-1}$ under $\partial_i$; with $\mathbf c_i$ the based cellular basis, set

$$\tau(C_*,\mathbf c)=\prod_i[\mathbf b_i,\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{i-1}/\mathbf c_i]^{(-1)^{i+1}}\in Q^\times,$$

where brackets denote the determinant of the change-of-basis matrix. The twisted Reidemeister torsion is this value modulo the subgroup $\mathcal U_{\rho,\psi}=\{\pm\det(\rho(g))\psi(g)^d:g\in G\}\subset Q^\times$. This exact determinant image is contained in the commonly used coarser unit subgroup $\{\pm a h:a\in\det(\rho(G)),\ h\in H\}$. The choice-free statement uses the full abelianization chain model first and specializes it only by the declared coefficient map $\chi$.

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice convention of the twisted-chain definition. Let $L$ be a nonempty oriented link, let $E_L$ be its chosen compact exterior, and let $X$ be a finite based two-dimensional CW complex with one $0$-cell, $n\ge2$ oriented $1$-cells $x_1,\ldots,x_n$, and $n-1$ oriented $2$-cells attached by based words $r_1,\ldots,r_{n-1}$. The supplied data include a based cellular spine certificate: a finite sequence of elementary cellular expansions and collapses identifying the simple-homotopy type of $X$ with the selected finite CW structure on $E_L$. Thus an abstract group isomorphism $\pi_1(X)\cong\pi_1(E_L)$ alone is not a spine certificate. Let $G=\pi_1(E_L)$, let $\rho:G\to\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb F)$ and $\psi:G\twoheadrightarrow H$ be the representation and declared free-abelian deck map, and put $Q=\operatorname{Frac}(\mathbb F[H])$. The associated deficiency-one presentation is $\langle x_1,\ldots,x_n\mid r_1,\ldots,r_{n-1}\rangle$ through the certified spine map. For $w\in F_n$, define Fox derivatives recursively by $\partial x_k/\partial x_j=\delta_{kj}$, $\partial(uv)/\partial x_j=\partial u/\partial x_j+u\,\partial v/\partial x_j$, and $\partial x_k^{-1}/\partial x_j=-x_k^{-1}\delta_{kj}$. Extend them linearly to the group ring and let $\Phi:\mathbb F[F_n]\to M_d(Q)$ be the ring homomorphism induced by $x_k\mapsto\rho(x_k)\psi(x_k)$. Form the block Fox matrix $J=(\Phi(\partial r_i/\partial x_k))_{i,k}$, of size $(n-1)d$ by $nd$. For a chosen column index $j$, let $J_{\widehat j}$ be obtained by deleting its entire $d$-column block and let $D_j=\det(\rho(x_j)\psi(x_j)-I_d)$. The Wada quotient for this column is defined only when $D_j\ne0$, and then is $W_j=\det(J_{\widehat j})/D_j\in Q$; a zero denominator makes that column inadmissible even when another column is valid. No abstract deficiency-one presentation is assigned exterior torsion unless its presentation complex is the stated based spine.

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice convention of the twisted-chain definition. Let $X$ be a connected finite based two-dimensional CW complex with one $0$-cell, $n\ge2$ $1$-cells and $n-1$ $2$-cells, so $\chi(X)=0$. Let $G=\pi_1(X)$, let $\psi:G\twoheadrightarrow H\cong\mathbb Z^m$ be an epimorphism with $m\ge1$, let $\rho:G\to\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb F)$ be a representation over a field, set $\Lambda=\mathbb F[H]$ and $Q=\operatorname{Frac}(\Lambda)$, and form the based twisted cellular complex from the preceding definition. If every element of $H_1(C_*^{\rho,\psi}(X;\Lambda^d))$ is annihilated by some nonzero element of $\Lambda$, then $C_*^{\rho,\psi}(X;Q^d)$ is acyclic. No assumption that its degree-two homology vanishes before localization is required.

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice convention of the twisted-chain definition. Let $X$ be a finite based CW model of a link exterior, let $G=\pi_1(X)$, let $\alpha(g)=\rho(g)\psi(g)\in\mathrm{GL}_d(Q)$ be its declared twisted coefficient representation, and suppose the based fraction-field complex is acyclic. Let $\mathcal U=\{\pm\det(\alpha(g)):g\in G\}$. Changing the lift or orientation of any cell multiplies the based Reidemeister torsion by an element of $\mathcal U$, so its class in $Q^\times/\mathcal U$ is unchanged. An elementary simple expansion or collapse, meaning addition or deletion of a pair of adjacent-dimensional cells whose lifted incidence block is $\pm g$ for some $g\in G$, has the same property.

Let $X$ be the based presentation $2$-complex with one vertex, oriented $1$-cells $x_1,\ldots,x_n$, and oriented $2$-cells attached along words $r_1,\ldots,r_m$ in the free group $F_n$. Let $G=\langle x_1,\ldots,x_n\mid r_1,\ldots,r_m\rangle$ be its presented fundamental group, let $\rho:G\to\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb F)$ be a representation, and let $\psi:G\to H$ be the declared free-abelian deck map. For $\Phi:\mathbb F[F_n]\to M_d(Q)$ induced by $x_j\mapsto\rho(x_j)\psi(x_j)$, the twisted differential $\partial_1$ has blocks $\rho(x_j)\psi(x_j)-I_d$, and the $i$th block row of $\partial_2$ is

$$\left(\Phi\left(\frac{\partial r_i}{\partial x_1}\right),\ldots,\Phi\left(\frac{\partial r_i}{\partial x_n}\right)\right),$$

where coefficient vectors are written as rows and differentials act on the right: the matrix of $\partial_1$ is the stacked column of blocks $\rho(x_j)\psi(x_j)-I_d$, while the matrix of $\partial_2$ is the $md$-by-$nd$ block matrix whose $i$th row is the displayed Fox row. The Fox derivatives use the product and inverse recursions in the Wada definition. Thus the evaluated Fox-Jacobian blocks are exactly the cellular boundary blocks of the based twisted complex of this presentation $2$-complex.

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice convention of the twisted-chain definition. Let $L$ be a nonempty oriented link and let $X$ be a certified finite based two-dimensional spine of its compact exterior with one $0$-cell, $n\ge2$ $1$-cells and $n-1$ $2$-cells. Let $\psi:\pi_1(X)\twoheadrightarrow H\cong\mathbb Z^m$ be an epimorphism with $m\ge1$, let $\rho:\pi_1(X)\to\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb F)$ be a representation over a field, and form the twisted chain complex over $\Lambda=\mathbb F[H]$ and its localization over $Q=\operatorname{Frac}(\Lambda)$. If its degree-one homology over $\Lambda$ is a torsion module, then its fraction-field complex is acyclic.

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice convention of the twisted-chain definition. Let $X$ be a certified based deficiency-one exterior spine with one $0$-cell, $n\ge2$ $1$-cells and $n-1$ $2$-cells, let $\psi:\pi_1(X)\twoheadrightarrow H\cong\mathbb Z^m$ have $m\ge1$, let $\rho:\pi_1(X)\to\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb F)$, and let $H_1(C_*^{\rho,\psi}(X;\mathbb F[H]^d))$ be torsion over $\mathbb F[H]$. Form the Fox block matrix $J$ and a chosen Wada column quotient $W_j=\det(J_{\widehat j})/D_j$ with $D_j=\det(\rho(x_j)\psi(x_j)-I_d)\ne0$. Then the fraction-field complex is acyclic, $\det(J_{\widehat j})\ne0$, and $W_j$ equals its based twisted Reidemeister torsion in $Q^\times/\mathcal U_{\rho,\psi}$. Every admissible deleted column gives the same class. This conclusion applies only to the specified cellular spine; an abstract presentation of the same group is insufficient.

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice convention of the twisted-chain definition. Let $K\subset S^3$ be an oriented knot, let $E_K$ be its compact exterior, let $X$ be a finite based deficiency-one two-dimensional spine with one vertex, $n\ge2$ oriented $1$-cells and $n-1$ oriented $2$-cells, certified by a based cellular simple-homotopy equivalence with $E_K$, and let $\psi:\pi_1(E_K)\twoheadrightarrow H\cong\mathbb Z^m$ have $m\ge1$. Let $\rho:\pi_1(E_K)\to\mathrm{GL}_d(\mathbb F)$ be a representation over a field, and assume the degree-one twisted homology over $\Lambda=\mathbb F[H]$ is a torsion module. For any admissible generator column of the Fox block matrix of the certified spine, its deleted-minor Wada quotient represents the based twisted Reidemeister torsion of $E_K$ in $Q^\times/\mathcal U_{\rho,\psi}$, where $Q=\operatorname{Frac}(\Lambda)$ and $\mathcal U_{\rho,\psi}=\{\pm\det(\rho(g))\psi(g)^d:g\in\pi_1(E_K)\}$. All admissible columns give the same class. If two such deficiency-one spines are related by a supplied finite based simple cellular equivalence carrying the same representation and deck map, their Wada quotient classes also agree. A group-presentation isomorphism alone is not such an equivalence.

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice convention of the twisted-chain definition. Let a finite colored geometric braid, a field with exact arithmetic, a representation of the closure exterior group, the full positive-meridian abelianization followed by a declared surjective color map, and compatible based spine and axis-filling certificates satisfy all input conditions of the colored twisted Burau procedure. Assume its designated denominator $D=\det(\rho(g_n)\psi(g_n)-I_d)$ is nonzero, so the procedure is applicable, and assume the representation and deck map extend over the filling with the axis meridian acting trivially. Then the procedure returns the class of the twisted Reidemeister torsion of the closure exterior. If the fraction-field complex is acyclic, the returned value is $N/D$, where $N=\det(\overline B_\rho(\beta)-I_{(n-1)d})$; if it is nonacyclic, the procedure returns $0$ and $N=0$, in agreement with the declared zero-torsion convention. The geometric certificates are essential hypotheses: matching a group presentation alone does not certify an exterior spine or the axis-filling decomposition.

items.statement: The assertion that every generator-column deletion gives a defined Wada quotient for a based deficiency-one spine is false. Let $X$ be the standard unknot exterior, with its circle spine generated by a positive meridian $y$, and form a based simple expansion by adding a $1$-cell $x$ and a $2$-cell attached by the word $r=x$. This gives the based deficiency-one presentation $\langle x,y\mid x\rangle$. Use the trivial one-dimensional representation over $\mathbb Q$ and the full abelianization deck map $\psi(x)=1$, $\psi(y)=t$ into $H=\langle t\rangle\cong\mathbb Z$. For the $x$ column, the Fox minor is $0$ and the denominator is $0$, so that column's Wada quotient is undefined; for the $y$ column, the denominator is $t-1\ne0$ and the quotient is $1/(t-1)$. Thus the invalidity of one designated column does not imply that another column is inadmissible.
